zoom.label: The block with large scrolls just below the bulls

c1.text: Level one: the bulls crowned a column. Now zoom to the block just below them.

zoom.label: The block with large scrolls just below the bulls

c1q.text: What is this block with large scrolls?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record AOD 1 (English page)
Marcel Dieulafoy, L'Acropole de Suse (1892; our translation)
R. Schmitt and D. Stronach, 'Apadāna', Encyclopaedia Iranica

c1a.text: Not the base: it sat high up, under the bulls.

correction.tempting: Column bases can be carved too.
correction.truth: It is the volute element that joined the bulls to the column shaft.

c1b.text: Yes. Inside the hall, a volute element joined the bulls to the shaft. The Louvre measures it as part of the capital, 3.2 metres high.

c1c.text: Not modern: the excavator measured this stone in the Louvre.

correction.truth: The volute element is ancient; the excavator measured it beside the bulls in 1892.

c1m.text: Scrolls between the bulls and the column.

zoom.label: The top of the capital, above the bulls' backs

c2.text: Level one: something heavy rested here. Now zoom to the top of the capital as it is shown today.

zoom.label: The top of the capital, above the bulls' backs

c2q.text: What lies across the bulls' backs today?

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 'Bull's head from column capital' (47.100.83)

c2a.text: Not stone: wood, as in the palace.

correction.tempting: The rest of the capital is stone.
correction.truth: The paired bulls carried wooden ceiling or roof beams; one is laid on them here.
correction.evidence: Encyclopaedia Iranica; Metropolitan Museum of Art.

c2b.text: Yes. A wooden beam lies on their backs, showing how the bulls carried the beams of the roof.

correction.tempting: It sits at the very top, like a roof.
correction.truth: The bulls carried wooden ceiling or roof beams; one lies on them here.
correction.evidence: Encyclopaedia Iranica; Metropolitan Museum of Art.

c2m.text: A wooden beam on stone bulls.

zoom.label: Both bull heads, from one side to the other

c3.text: Level one: the hall was vast. Now zoom out across both heads.

zoom.label: Both bull heads, from one side to the other

c3q.text: How wide is the pair, forehead to forehead?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record AOD 1 (English page)
Marcel Dieulafoy, L'Acropole de Suse (1892; our translation)

correction.tempting: In a photo it looks like one column top.
correction.truth: The Louvre and the excavator both measured 3.74 metres.

c3b.text: Too wide: less than half that.

correction.tempting: The columns were about 20 metres tall.
correction.truth: The pair measures 3.74 metres across the foreheads.

c3c.text: Yes. The pair measures 3.74 metres across the foreheads, as wide as a small room.

extends.concept: From "the bulls crowned a column" (level) to how the crown was built: a volute element under the bulls

c1q.what_you_learn: The scrolled block is the volute element of the capital, joining the bulls to the shaft.

c1q.confidence: Medium-high: the Louvre and Marcel Dieulafoy both measure the volute element as part of the capital (3.20 m); Dieulafoy and Stronach describe the composite capital of the hall. How exactly the two parts fit (232 + 320 cm against 532 cm in all) is TBD and is not asked.
c1q.notes: Ledger ca-005, ca-018. The number of volutes (sixteen, Dieulafoy only) is not used.
